text:
maria: Heads-up — premerge SAST job #8843 failed on main with ~12 findings and the CI artifact decrypt failed. Also seeing a KMS audit gap around the same time. Not sure if this blocks the release.
kevin: CI link: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/8843 — logs attached.
lee: quick summary from logs:
```
Error: decrypt failed: access denied
kms: request_id=abcd1234, principal=ci-service-account@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
lee: I pulled KMS audit logs; I see no decrypt event for that principal at 2026-03-20T10:23:xxZ. There are decrypt events but from `ci-runner@infra`.
maria: So principal mismatch. Could be RBAC change or an ephemeral token swap. @sre-oncall can you verify which SA the runner used during that build?
sre-oncall: checking now — build metadata says `ci-service-account` but the KMS logs show decrypts from `ci-runner@infra` earlier and then an AccessDenied for `ci-service-account`.
kevin: We had PR #492 this week which changed CI bindings. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/492 — it removed ``roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`` from `ci-service-account` and consolidated to `ci-runner`.
maria: That explains the AccessDenied. Two things to decide: revert the PR or add a temporary backfill to restore decrypt rights for `ci-service-account` until we fully flip the runner SA.
lee: Proposed triage plan:
1) Short-term: grant `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` back to `ci-service-account` scoped to the key used, for one hour. (so we can rerun and collect evidence)
2) Rerun SAST/DAST and collect ALL KMS audit snippets + build logs.
3) If SAST high findings are true positives, owners fix before release; low findings can be suppressed with evidence and an exemption ticket.
maria: On the SAST findings: some look like real SQLi patterns from generated test inputs, others look like detector false positives in templated code.
security-bot: SEC-412 created: "CI artifact decrypt failure + SAST/DAST triage". Assigned to maria, kevin. Please attach KMS audit snippets and build id.
kevin: I'll take the two `HIGH` SAST alerts (sql-injection-ish). maria, can you triage the rest (medium/low) and flag anything that blocks?
maria: Yep. I'll also run a local harness to reproduce; quick trick: set `MOCK_DA=true` to avoid DAST flakiness when reproducing.
sre-oncall: Done temporary grant to `ci-service-account` for key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/artifacts-key` (1h). Rerun triggered.
ci-bot: Re-run triggered: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/8843?rerun=1
lee: While rerun happens, save these audit snippets into SEC-412. Example snippet to capture (from KMS logs):
```
protoPayload.methodName: "google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail: "ci-service-account@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
```
maria: If rerun still shows AccessDenied, then we reopen infra PR and revert. But if rerun succeeds and SAST findings persist, proceed with normal security review.
kevin: For documentation: add a short note in the premerge playbook about "validate KMS principal used by CI" — I can open a follow-up doc PR.
security-bot: Note added to SEC-412: "capture KMS audit, attach build log, assign evidence owner".
maria: Thanks all. After rerun, I'll attach the KMS evidence and initial triage notes. If any HIGH is confirmed, ping @sec-review for a quick 30-min review window.
lee: One more: we should add an automated CI check that flags mismatched principals between build metadata and recent KMS decrypt audit entries (low-cost detector). Filing a tech debt ticket.
maria: Ack. I'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
